title: Open-source AI week — OpenViking, ARTEMIS, GLM-5.3 FlashX, Unsloth Studio
summary: Six releases in 60 seconds: OpenViking (context database for agent memory), Google's ARTEMIS (prompt-to-phone automation over MCP for Codex, Claude Code and Antigravity), PrismML Ternary Bonsai 2 (27B ternary reasoning model, 262k context), AWS Pizza Bot (email-style inbox for background agents), Z.ai GLM-5.3 FlashX (320B multimodal, 1M context, local), and Unsloth Studio no-code fine-tuning of 500+ models in free Colab.
takeaways: OpenViking gives agents one store for knowledge, user memory and reusable experience
ARTEMIS exposes phone automation to coding agents via MCP
Unsloth Studio fine-tunes open models in free Colab without code
Ternary compression makes 27B reasoning models laptop-sized

title: DuckStation 3D screenshot — rip any PS1 scene to OBJ for Blender
summary: A DuckStation fork with a 3D-screenshot feature dumps the current PS1 scene as an OBJ with positions intact, ready to drag into Blender. More reliable than the older Avocado emulator route, which had vertex and texture bugs. The creator turns rips into papercraft models.
takeaways: Use the DuckStation 3D-screenshot fork from GitHub, not Avocado
Screenshots land as OBJ in a screenshot-3D folder
Extracted meshes keep scene placement, good for dioramas or papercraft

title: Open vs closed token share — Friedberg on the 12-week flip and Anthropic risk
summary: David Friedberg on All-In says token usage flipped from 80/20 closed-to-open to 80/20 open-to-closed in 12 weeks, calling it Anthropic's biggest risk factor ahead of S-1s. He expects a bifurcated market: open weights for most use, premium models for hard engineering, math and biology work.
takeaways: Open-weight models now dominate token volume per Friedberg's chart
Premium closed models keep pricing power on hard technical work
Open weights are spreading into robotics VLAs and image/video

title: ln + vpype — 3D scenes to hidden-line vector art for pen plotters
summary: Michael Fogleman's ln (Go) renders 3D scenes as 2D vector paths by ray-testing each path segment for visibility, supporting CSG, math surfaces and procedural cities. vpype then merges and sorts paths for plotting, cutting pen-up travel 86% in this example. Both MIT licensed, output straight to SVG.
takeaways: ln outputs vector paths, not pixels, so 3D scenes plot in real ink
vpype linemerge + linesort drastically cuts pen-up travel
Texture is defined by which paths you put on a surface
Animate a moving camera for line-art animation

title: Quake III fast inverse square root — the 0x5f3759df bit hack explained
summary: Explains Quake III's four-line fast inverse square root: reinterpret float bits as an integer (which behaves logarithmically), shift right to halve the exponent, subtract from magic constant 0x5f3759df, then one Newton-Raphson step to bring error under 0.175%. Covers why normalization was costly on 1999 Pentiums and the constant's lineage through 3dfx and Cleve Moler.
takeaways: Float bits read as an integer approximate a logarithm
One Newton-Raphson pass turns a 1% approximation into under 0.18%
The constant balances exponent bias 127 against linear error

title: AI game decompilation hype — Mario/Halo merges and PS5 piracy rumors
summary: Rumor-heavy rant claiming AI decompilation is letting people merge games like Mario 64 and Halo, pirate Adobe software, port the PS5 library to PC, and leak GTA 6. Mostly unverified claims plus a piracy justification, with no technical detail.
takeaways: Unverified claims, treat as noise
The real trend underneath is AI-assisted decompilation

title: Google game Playground — why a harness that can't see its output fails
summary: A hands-on review of Google's prompt-to-game Playground: output ignored the supplied concept art, the model denied receiving it, and it admitted it cannot see or play the games it builds. The takeaway is that a game-building harness needs visual verification and playtesting.
takeaways: Agent harnesses for visual work need a way to see and test the output
Without feedback loops, generated games ignore reference art
Paid tool, low quality per this test

title: Founder OS — 17 always-on AI agents running a one-person business
summary: Tour of a custom Founder OS dashboard: 17 agents on a Mac Mini covering comms, sales, finance, marketing and clients, with a skills tree, task panel, workflow builder, Trackio lead attribution and a 'wizard' conductor agent. The base Founder OS is described as open source with a waitlist.
takeaways: Organize agents by business department with shared company context
A single conductor agent keeps the fleet coordinated
Centralize comms and lead tracking into the same system

title: AgentCraft — Minecraft mod where Claude agents write real code
summary: An open-source Minecraft mod built on Claude's agent system: a Foreman tracks tasks, ordering, decisions and inter-agent messages, workers each get an isolated copy of the code, and nothing merges until approved. Agents commit under their own names and can be messaged mid-task, and they walk over to find you when they need input.
takeaways: Give each worker agent an isolated code copy and gate merges on approval
Per-agent commit identities make blame and review easy
A coordinator that logs decisions prevents agents re-litigating work
Spatial UIs can make agent activity legible

title: Whop neobank blueprint — one-click fintech with cards and crypto rails
summary: Sponsored Whop promo: a 'neobank blueprint' that spins up virtual cards, balances, crypto deposits, payouts and transfers, with fees you collect per swipe or transfer. Framed as cloning Coinbase in five minutes, which it is not.
takeaways: Sponsored content, verify compliance and custody before relying on it
Whop bundles card issuing and crypto rails as a template

title: GPT-6 Astra side hustles — ten money-making uses, no detail
summary: A silent video promising ten ways to make money with GPT-6 Astra. No transcript or slide text survives, so there is nothing to act on.
takeaways: No extractable content
Low-signal save, keep only as a trend marker

title: Anti-surveillance OPSEC tools — plate-reader confusion and photo poisoning
summary: Three privacy tools: license-plate marks that make Flock and ALPR cameras misread your plate, an image cloaking tool that poisons photos against face models and deepfakes, and a list of 78 ranked ways to evade AI surveillance. Links are comment-gated. Note that altering plates is illegal in many places.
takeaways: Image cloaking tools perturb photos to break face-model training
Plate modification carries legal risk
A ranked list of 78 counter-surveillance methods exists

title: AI networking for job referrals — archetype-based LinkedIn outreach
summary: Have an AI export your LinkedIn connections, find newly hired or promoted people via a sales data tool, classify each into four personality archetypes from their profile and posts, then draft outreach tailored to each. Prompts are comment-gated.
takeaways: Target recently hired or promoted people, they are most open
Match message tone to the recipient's archetype
Referrals beat cold applications

title: Self-improving trading agent — critic loop that rewrites losing strategies
summary: Workflow pitch: describe a strategy, an agent codes it and wires the broker API, runs a five-year backtest, and a critic agent dissects losing trades and rewrites entry/exit logic before rerunning. Hard-coded stop-loss and drawdown limits sit outside the agent's reach, and failed strategies go to a local DB the agent learns from. Guide is comment-gated.
takeaways: Lock risk limits in code the agent cannot modify
Store failed strategies so the agent avoids repeating them
Beware overfitting when an agent rewrites rules to fix past losers

title: DLSS 5 mod wave — frame gen and neural rendering unlocked on older RTX
summary: Roundup of community mods enabling DLSS 5 and frame generation on RTX 20/30/40 cards, first via an FSR redirect then a native FrameGen proxy, plus an OptiScaler fork that runs neural rendering before upscaling for up to 50% more FPS. DLSS 5 Autopilot on GitHub bundles the tools, and dual-GPU offload of neural rendering is demoed. Mods can trip anti-cheat.
takeaways: DLSS 5 frame gen runs on RTX 20-40 via proxy mods
Ordering neural rendering before upscaling boosts FPS
Anti-cheat may flag these mods in online games

title: Impeccable skill + Three.js — three-part stack for premium AI-built websites
summary: Recipe for one-shot polished websites with Claude: the Impeccable skill (generate variations then refine with its 23 design sub-skills), an image or video generator such as GPT Image 2.5 or Seedance 2.5 for visuals, and Three.js for smooth animation and transitions.
takeaways: One strong design skill beats a pile of skills
Generate multiple variations and refine the best
Real imagery and motion are what make sites feel premium

title: Five Python 1DTE options bots — visualized as a live trading city
summary: A trader runs five rule-based Python bots on QQQ, SPY and IWM one-day-to-expiry options, visualized as a city where each tower shows signals and fires on call/put entries. Strategies are 'trending' and 'OG' with a daily profit lock. P&L claims ($72k in a month) are unverified.
takeaways: Rule-based bots remove emotional trading
A daily profit lock caps give-back
Visualizing bot state makes live monitoring more legible

title: GLM-5.3 Hugging Face takedown — Pirate Face mirrors and model access fights
summary: News mix: Hugging Face disabled a modified GLM-5.3 listing and Pirate Face claims a decentralized mirror. PewDiePie reports OpenAI bans while distilling his Ajax model, and Anthropic research says GLM-5.3 approached Claude Mythos Preview on exploit-development tests. The video pushes cracked-model links, so treat with caution.
takeaways: Platform takedowns of modified open weights are increasing
Distilling from closed APIs can get accounts banned
Cracked-model mirrors are a security risk

title: Claude trading watcher — LiquidTrade + QuiverQuant for insider-trade alerts
summary: Connect Claude to LiquidTrade for brokerage access across stocks, crypto, forex and prediction markets, and QuiverQuant for insider, politician and institutional trade data. Then give it a rule like tracking an investor's disclosures, compare against your portfolio, run it as a recurring routine, and paper trade first.
takeaways: QuiverQuant exposes insider, congressional and institutional flows
Use routines so Claude checks for new disclosures automatically
Paper trade before any real money

title: Jev keyword triage — score SERP beatability before writing content
summary: Pull the top 10 results for 72 keywords and have TypeSafe's Jev (a classifier model that returns probabilities) answer literal questions per result: intent match, depth, freshness, site strength, beatable or not. Three or more weak results means target the keyword, then Claude writes. 720 results cost about 4 cents, search volume still needs a separate tool.
takeaways: Pick keywords by how beatable page one is, not by volume
Ask literal yes/no questions for clean classifier answers
Three or more weak top-10 results marks a winnable keyword
Manually review results the model was unsure about

title: Fish Audio phone agent — AI receptionist that gathers context then hands off
summary: A support line where a Fish Audio voice agent on a Twilio number discloses it is AI, asks consent to take notes, collects context into database tables, then calls you, briefs you and merges the call. Repeat callers get their history recalled. The agent never tries to resolve issues itself, avoiding Taco Bell-style failures.
takeaways: Use the voice agent for intake and context, not resolution
Disclose AI and ask consent for notes upfront
Brief the human then merge calls to cut resolution time
Persist caller context for repeat calls

title: Browser spy-satellite OSINT map — 19 live layers with voice control
summary: A trending GitHub repo offering a 3D browser globe with 19 live data layers like public CCTV, Flock camera locations and traffic, plus a Jarvis-style voice interface. You can fly to a city or click a live flight to view a simulated cockpit perspective. Link is comment-gated.
takeaways: Public CCTV, ALPR and traffic feeds can be fused on one map
Useful reference for building geospatial dashboards

title: Chat-history mining — derive better custom instructions from your AI logs
summary: Export your full ChatGPT or Claude history, have a small model like Jev tag every conversation for mistakes and usage patterns, then feed the analysis to your main assistant to write new custom instructions. A cheaper alternative to building a full personal 'Jarvis' agent.
takeaways: Your exported chat history is the best personalization dataset
Use a cheap model to tag errors and usage at scale
Turn the analysis into custom instructions
